s0003.literal: Zhou Hongzheng; younger brother Hongzhi; Hongzhi's son Que; Yuan Xian
s0003.idiomatic: Zhou Hongzheng; his younger brother Hongzhi; Hongzhi's son Que; Yuan Xian

s0004.literal: Zhou Hongzheng, styled Sixing, was a native of Ancheng in Runan.
s0004.idiomatic: Zhou Hongzheng, styled Sixing, came from Ancheng in Runan.

s0006.literal: Editorial footnote marker 1. a ninth-generation descendant of Yan, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of Jin.
s0006.idiomatic: [1] He was a ninth-generation descendant of Yan, grand master of splendid happiness under Jin.

s0007.literal: His grandfather Yan was Secretariat Gentleman of Qi and concurrently headed the Bureau of Writings.
s0007.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan had been a secretariat gentleman under Qi and head of the Bureau of Writings.

s0008.literal: His father Baoshi was libationer to the Minister of Education under Liang.
s0008.idiomatic: His father Baoshi had served Liang as libationer to the minister of education.

s0009.literal: Hongzheng lost his father young; with his younger brothers Hongrang and Hongzhi he was all
s0009.idiomatic: Hongzheng was orphaned young. He and his younger brothers Hongrang and Hongzhi were all

s0011.literal: [elder] uncle, Palace Attendant and General Who Protects the Army She, who raised them.
s0011.idiomatic: raised by their paternal uncle She, palace attendant and general who protects the army.

s0012.literal: Editorial footnote marker 2. At age ten he had mastered the Laozi and the Book of Changes; whenever She discussed them with him he marveled and said, "Judging by your expression, you are quick and bright, your mind clear and alert; if you become famous in later generations, you will surpass me."
s0012.idiomatic: [2] At ten he had mastered the Laozi and the Book of Changes. Whenever She debated them with him, She would marvel and say, "Your face is quick and bright, your mind clear and alert. If you become famous later, you will surpass me."

s0013.literal: Pei Ziye of Hedong deeply admired and accepted him and asked to give him his daughter in marriage.
s0013.idiomatic: Pei Ziye of Hedong admired him deeply and asked for his daughter's hand in marriage.

s0014.literal: At fifteen he was summoned to fill a vacancy as a National University student; he also lectured on the Book of Changes at the National Academy, and the students transmitted and studied his interpretations.
s0014.idiomatic: At fifteen he was made a student of the National University and lectured on the Book of Changes there; the students took up his readings.

s0015.literal: He entered study in the last month of spring and in the first month of winter sought to sit for the examination; the academic office, because his time was short, would not permit it.
s0015.idiomatic: He entered in late spring and in early winter sought to sit for the examination, but the academic office refused him because he had not been there long enough.

s0016.literal: Doctor Dao Qia deliberated and said, "Master Zhou is not yet of weak-crown age yet already expounds a classic himself; though called a student, he is truly fit to be a teacher and model—there is no need to wait for a written examination."
s0016.idiomatic: Doctor Dao Qia argued, "Young Zhou is not yet twenty yet already teaches a classic himself. Though called a student, he is fit to be a teacher. There is no need for a written examination."

s0017.literal: He began his career as Erudite of the Imperial University under Liang.
s0017.idiomatic: He began his career as erudite of the imperial university under Liang.

s0018.literal: When the Prince of Jin'an was governor of Danyang, [Hongzheng] was summoned as chief clerk.
s0018.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin'an governed Danyang, Hongzheng was made his chief clerk.

s0019.literal: He went out as magistrate of Ye county; Editorial footnote marker 3. on his mother's death he left office.
s0019.idiomatic: He was posted as magistrate of Ye county. [3] When his mother died he left office.

s0020.literal: When mourning ended he successively served as magistrate of Qu'e and Anji.
s0020.idiomatic: After mourning he served in turn as magistrate of Qu'e and Anji.

s0021.literal: In the Putong era the office of Clerk for Literary Righteousness was first established; attached to the Shouguang Office, Hongzheng was made Vice Director for Righteousness.
s0021.idiomatic: In the Putong era the post of clerk for literary righteousness was created. Hongzheng was made vice director, attached to the Shouguang Office.

s0022.literal: I have heard that the image of yielding and modesty arose with the trigrams of Xi and Xuan, and the source of bowing and yielding was born in the abdications of Yao and Shun; it is of long standing and can be set forth in detail.
s0022.idiomatic: I have heard that the image of yielding and modesty arose with the trigrams of Xi and Xuan, and that bowing and yielding began with the abdications of Yao and Shun. The tradition is ancient and can be traced in detail.

s0023.literal: The temple hall and the Fen River were different paths yet one return; Ji, Qi, Chao, and Xu were different names yet one thread—those who went out were called chief, those who remained were called outer ministers; none failed to support inner and outer, form governance in surface and core; this was the same rule for ten thousand generations and what the hundred kings did not change.
s0023.idiomatic: Temple and Fen River were different roads to the same end; Ji, Qi, Chao, and Xu were different names for the same principle. Those who served at court were called chiefs; those who withdrew were outer ministers. Inner and outer always supported each other until government was whole. That was the rule for all ages, unchanged by the hundred kings.

s0024.literal: By the age of the Three Kings it gradually declined; each honored his own kin, each favored his own son.
s0024.idiomatic: By the age of the Three Kings it had already declined: each man honored only his own kin and favored only his own son.

s0025.literal: Down to the Seven States contending and Liu and Xiang racing in pursuit, Han fanned the custom and Jin raised the wave; the way of yielding was abandoned for many years.
s0025.idiomatic: Then came the warring of the Seven States and the race of Liu and Xiang. Han fanned the fashion and Jin raised the wave. The way of yielding was cast aside for generations.

s0026.literal: Pattern and substance alternate in change; the thin and the pure reform each other; to return to simplicity and turn back to antiquity—now is the time.
s0026.idiomatic: Ornament and substance take turns; the corrupt and the pure replace one another. To return to simplicity and turn back to antiquity—now is the time.

s0027.literal: I bow before the Illustrious Great King's Highness: Heaven has drawn forth your near-sagehood, bright and divine in martial power; the hundred offices are your crown, the four seas return to benevolence.
s0027.idiomatic: I bow before Your Illustrious Highness: Heaven has drawn you forth as a near-sage, bright and martial. The hundred offices are your crown; the four seas return to your benevolence.

s0028.literal: Therefore the Emperor has issued virtuous words and sent down a clear edict, making Your Highness the state's heir and the root of all under Heaven.
s0028.idiomatic: Therefore the Emperor has issued virtuous words and sent down a clear edict making you heir to the state—the root of all under Heaven.

s0029.literal: Though one recall Xia Qi, Zhou Song, the Han heir, and the two Wei heirs—can such rulers be mentioned in the same breath as Your Highness?
s0029.idiomatic: Even Xia Qi, Zhou Song, the Han heir, and the two Wei heirs—what are such men beside Your Highness?

s0030.literal: My thought is that I would hear Your Highness lift your eyes to the yielding of Boyi above and hold to the great worth's conduct of Zizang; flee the jade carriage and not ride it, cast away the ten thousand chariots as one casts off shoes—perhaps to change the custom of shallow rivalry and enlarge the wind of great Wu.
s0030.idiomatic: I would have Your Highness lift your eyes to Boyi's yielding and hold to the great worth Zizang's example: flee the jade carriage and refuse to mount it, cast off the realm as one casts off a shoe—perhaps to change shallow rivalry and restore the great wind of Wu.

s0031.literal: Antiquity had such men; today we hear such words; he who can act on them—who if not Your Highness?
s0031.idiomatic: Antiquity had such men; today we hear such words. Who can act on them if not Your Highness?

s0032.literal: He could make the transformation of non-action revive in
s0032.idiomatic: He could make the rule of non-action rise again in

s0034.literal: [remote] antiquity; Editorial footnote marker 5. the way of yielding kings would not fall in ages to come—would it not be glorious!
s0034.idiomatic: [remote] antiquity. [5] The way of yielding kings would not fall in ages to come—would it not be glorious!

s0036.literal: Hongzheng is a shabby student of shallow learning, ashamed before antiquity in righteousness; his house is from Ru and Ying, for generations transmitting loyal fierceness; his forebear Yan, clerk of the Decision Office, resisted with words in nine remonstrances, lofty in conduct before the ten-thousand-chariot lord, stern in countenance before the three bureaus—though the work of flourishing virtue was about to end, the wind of blunt uprightness had not fallen.
s0036.idiomatic: Hongzheng is a shabby scholar, ashamed before the ancients. His house comes from Ru and Ying and for generations has transmitted fierce loyalty. His forebear Yan, clerk of the Decision Office, spoke out in nine remonstrances, held lofty conduct before the throne, and kept stern countenance before the three bureaus. Though great virtue was ending, the wind of blunt uprightness had not fallen.

s0037.literal: Therefore I dare lay open my inmost heart and display my foolish blindness.
s0037.idiomatic: Therefore I dare lay open my heart and show my foolishness.

s0038.literal: If my rustic words and wild sayings might briefly reach your hearing, though I should cast my body beneath the cauldron or meet death on the lung-stone, on the day I die I would still be as on the day I lived.
s0038.idiomatic: If these rustic words might briefly reach your ear, though I should die beneath the cauldron or on the execution stone, on the day of my death I would still count myself alive.

s0039.literal: His outspoken integrity and upright guarding of principle were all of this kind.
s0039.idiomatic: His outspoken integrity and upright conduct were all of this kind.

s0040.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the National University.
s0040.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to erudite of the National University.

s0041.literal: At that time the Forest of Scholars Hall was established west of the city; Hongzheng dwelt there to lecture, and listeners filled court and countryside.
s0041.idiomatic: At that time the Forest of Scholars Hall was built west of the city. Hongzheng lived there to teach, and listeners filled court and countryside.

s0042.literal: Hongzheng submitted to Emperor Wu of Liang fifty items of doubtful points in the Book of Changes, and also asked to explain the two Appended Phrases on Qian and Kun, saying: "Your servant has heard that the Changes says, 'Establish images to exhaust meaning; attach words to exhaust speech'—then one knows the sage's feeling and the subtle can be seen.
s0042.idiomatic: Hongzheng submitted to Emperor Wu of Liang fifty doubtful points on the Book of Changes and asked to explain the two Appended Phrases on Qian and Kun. He said, "I have heard that the Changes says, 'Establish images to exhaust meaning; attach words to exhaust speech'—then the sage's feeling may be known and the subtle seen.

s0043.literal: Unless one embraces the subtle, embodies the utmost, exhausts transformation and probes spirit, how can one penetrate intent and accomplish tasks, plumb the hidden and reach afar?
s0043.idiomatic: Unless one embraces the subtle, embodies the utmost, and exhausts transformation and spirit, how can one penetrate intent, accomplish tasks, and reach the hidden afar?

s0044.literal: Yet Confucius compared it to fetters and broke the leather thongs at the lacquered characters; what Xuanyuan heard and polished, he left the dark pearl in Red Water.
s0044.idiomatic: Yet Confucius called it fetters and broke the leather cords at the lacquered text; what the Yellow Emperor polished, he left as the dark pearl in Red Water.

s0045.literal: I bow before Your Majesty's ten thousand affairs in a day, not taxing spirit in an instant; you concentrate mind on the subtle root and constantly attain the natural truth; sage wisdom cannot hide its subtle depths, bright spirit cannot sink into what cannot be fathomed.
s0045.idiomatic: I bow before Your Majesty, who handles ten thousand affairs in a day without taxing your spirit in an instant; who concentrates on the subtle root and constantly attains natural truth; whose sage wisdom cannot hide its depths and whose bright spirit cannot be lost in the unfathomable.

s0046.literal: As for the trigrams wrapped in the Six Classics and words exhausted in the two Appended Phrases—famous scholars debated heatedly for years, great scholars clapped hands for a year end—none tried to wander their outer fence, none ever saw their far shore.
s0046.idiomatic: As for the trigrams wrapped in the Six Classics and the words exhausted in the two Appended Phrases—famous scholars debated for years, great scholars talked for a year end—none had tried their outer fence, none had seen their far shore.

s0047.literal: Since Your Majesty's own instructions descended in discussion and shaped the Way of the Changes, splitting the utmost subtle to an autumn down and melting layered ice in a dark valley.
s0047.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's own instructions came down and shaped the Way of the Changes, splitting the utmost subtle to an autumn down and melting layered ice in a dark valley.

s0048.literal: Your servant personally received the tone and intent and had the duty of proclaiming and transmitting; the later students were numerous and not without transmitted learning.
s0048.idiomatic: Your servant personally received your tone and intent and had the duty of proclaiming it; the later students were many and not without a transmitted school.

s0049.literal: But the profundity of Qian and Kun was not yet opened, the subtlety of the Appended Tables not yet explained, so that one classic's deep reach still left much doubt.
s0049.idiomatic: But the profundity of Qian and Kun was not yet opened and the subtlety of the Appended Tables not yet explained, so that one classic's deep reach still left much doubt.

s0050.literal: Your servant, not measuring his shallowness, lightly and rashly short and crude, respectfully together with his students Zhang Ji of Qinghe and three hundred twelve others, on the image-lines of Qian and Kun and the two Appended Phrases not yet opened, bow and hope in the leisure of your hearing you will bend to instruct—so that your humble servant may drill and look up and complete his earnest study, and later generations who love the matter may have a lineage to uphold.
s0050.idiomatic: Your servant, not measuring his shallowness, respectfully joins Zhang Ji of Qinghe and three hundred twelve fellow students. On the image-lines of Qian and Kun and the two Appended Phrases, which are not yet opened, we bow and hope that in the leisure of your hearing you will instruct us—so that we may study in earnest and later generations who love learning may have a school to uphold.

s0051.literal: Reflecting on my great fortune, I rejoice to bathe in the Way in the years of Yao; I study to the end of life and do not know old age is coming.
s0051.idiomatic: Reflecting on my great fortune, I rejoice to bathe in the Way in an age like Yao's; I study all my life and do not know that old age is coming.

s0052.literal: Heaven's honor does not hear, yet I rashly submit this request; ice and valley fill my breast and I know not where to place myself."
s0052.idiomatic: Heaven's honor does not hear, yet I rashly submit this request. Ice and valley fill my breast and I know not where to turn."

s0053.literal: An edict replied: "Setting hexagrams and observing images—the matter is remote and the text high; composing the Appended Phrases and displaying words—the phrasing is deep and the principle abstruse. The thought of the silken cords cut in eastern Lu, the writing in western Bo's deep sorrow—the matter exceeds the Three Antiquities, men have changed through seven sages. From Shang Qu's receiving and Ziyong's transmitting, the bamboo slips were drowned and the years far away.
s0053.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Setting hexagrams and observing images—the matter is remote and the text lofty; composing the Appended Phrases—the words are deep and the principle abstruse. The thought of cut silken cords in eastern Lu, the writing in western Bo's deep sorrow—the matter exceeds the Three Antiquities; men have changed through seven sages. From Shang Qu's receiving and Ziyong's transmitting, the slips were lost and the years far away.

s0054.literal: Master Tian won fame in Zichuan; Liangqiu excelled in Langye learning; Master Fan of Dai commandery and the Wang clan of Shanyang—men hid the treasure of Jing Mountain; each exhausted the flavor of dark speech; explanations differed in what they took or left and intent had detail or brevity.
s0054.idiomatic: Master Tian won fame in Zichuan; Liangqiu excelled in Langye; Master Fan of Dai and the Wang of Shanyang—each hid the treasure of Jing Mountain and exhausted the flavor of dark learning. Explanations differed in what they kept or dropped; intent had its detail and brevity.

s0055.literal: Recently gentry learning all had doubts to examine; answering each question, separate explanations have already been prepared.
s0055.idiomatic: Recently the learning of the gentry has had doubts to examine; answers to each question have already been prepared in separate explanations.

s0056.literal: I know that you and Zhang Ji and three hundred twelve others need the words of the Wenyan on Qian and Kun and the two Appended Phrases explained; when the ten thousand affairs allow a little leisure, I will try to discuss them."
s0056.idiomatic: I know that you and Zhang Ji and three hundred twelve others need the Wenyan on Qian and Kun and the two Appended Phrases explained. When the ten thousand affairs allow a little leisure, I will try to discuss them."

s0057.literal: Hongzheng was broadly learned and knew dark images; he was skilled at divination and observation.
s0057.idiomatic: Hongzheng was broadly learned and knew the dark images; he was skilled at divination and observation.

s0058.literal: At the end of Datong he once told his younger brother Hongrang: "The state's fortune is ill; in a few years there will be war rising—we and you do not know where to flee."
s0058.idiomatic: Near the end of Datong he once told his younger brother Hongrang, "The state's fortune is ill. In a few years war will rise—we do not know where we shall flee."

s0059.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang received Hou Jing, Hongzheng told Hongrang: "The stair of disorder is here."
s0059.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang received Hou Jing, Hongzheng told Hongrang, "The stair of disorder starts here."

s0060.literal: When the capital fell, Hongzhi was Administrator of Hengyang; Emperor Yuan was at Jiangling and sent Hongzhi a letter saying: "There is just now capital news: your worthy elder brother the Erudite is safe.
s0060.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Hongzhi was administrator of Hengyang. Emperor Yuan was at Jiangling and sent Hongzhi a letter: "There is capital news: your worthy elder brother the erudite is safe.

s0061.literal: But the gentry of the capital, none failed to join the rebels; Wang Ke had become a household servant, Lu Mian's body filled the ranks of soldiers—only Master Zhou stood firm and unbending.
s0061.idiomatic: But of the capital gentry none failed to join the rebels. Wang Ke had become a household servant; Lu Mian's body filled the ranks of soldiers. Only Master Zhou stood firm and unbending.

s0062.literal: Speaking of the western army, his tears flowed like a stream; he constantly longed for my coming as one longs for harvest; of pines and cypresses that wither last—he alone.
s0062.idiomatic: Speaking of the western army, his tears flowed like a stream. He constantly longed for my coming as one longs for harvest. Of pines and cypresses that wither last—he alone.

s0063.literal: When Wang Sengbian campaigned against Hou Jing, Hongzheng and Hongrang broke out on their own to welcome the army; Sengbian was greatly pleased and that same day reported to Emperor Yuan; Emperor Yuan wrote Hongzheng in his own hand: "The savage ugliness rebelled and disorder separated cold and heat again and again; acquaintances within the seas were nearly all gone.
s0063.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian campaigned against Hou Jing, Hongzheng and Hongrang broke out on their own to welcome his army. Sengbian was greatly pleased and that day reported to Emperor Yuan. Emperor Yuan wrote Hongzheng in his own hand: "The savage rebel has torn cold from heat again and again; acquaintances within the seas are nearly all gone.

s0064.literal: Han Fei's wisdom did not escape Qin's prison; Liu Xin's learning still perished in Xin; voice and dust do not continue—I am often burning with grief.
s0064.idiomatic: Han Fei's wisdom did not escape Qin's prison; Liu Xin's learning still perished in Xin. Voice and dust do not continue—I burn with grief.

s0065.literal: I have often wished to visit Shandong to seek Ziyun and ask west of the Pass for Boqi; meeting this present letter, I attach it with all my strength; I await the coming post to comfort my long waiting."
s0065.idiomatic: I have often wished to visit Shandong to seek Ziyun and ask west of the Pass for Boqi. Meeting this present letter, I send word with all my strength and await the coming post to comfort my long waiting."

s0066.literal: He then sent an envoy to welcome him and told the court gentlemen: "When the Jin house pacified Wu, they rejoiced to gain the two Lus; now in breaking the bandit I too have gained the two Zhous—one time in ancient and modern, enough to be paired."
s0066.idiomatic: He then sent an envoy to welcome him and told the court gentlemen, "When the Jin house pacified Wu, they rejoiced to gain the two Lus. Now in breaking the bandit I too have gained the two Zhous—ancient and modern in one moment, enough to be paired."

s0067.literal: When Hongzheng arrived, the ritual and courtesy were very generous; no court minister could compare.
s0067.idiomatic: When Hongzheng arrived, the honors were very generous; no court minister could compare.

s0068.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and attached to the Secretariat.
s0068.idiomatic: He was made gentleman of the yellow gate, attached to the secretariat.

s0069.literal: Soon he was promoted to Minister of the Left for the People and shortly after made supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
s0069.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to minister of the left for the people and shortly after made supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

s0070.literal: Emperor Yuan once wrote in the Golden Tower Master: "Among monks I value Master Yan of Zhaoti; among recluses I value Tao Zhenbai of Huayang; among gentry I value Zhou Hongzheng of Runan—in reasoning, clear and inexhaustible; he too is a famous scholar of the age."
s0070.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan once wrote in the Golden Tower Master: "Among monks I value Master Yan of Zhaoti; among recluses Tao Zhenbai of Huayang; among gentry Zhou Hongzheng of Runan—in reasoning, clear and inexhaustible. He too is a famous scholar of the age."

s0071.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Sengbian reported and sent the secretariat's books and registers; an edict ordered Hongzheng to collate them.
s0071.idiomatic: When Hou Jing was pacified, Sengbian reported and sent the secretariat's books and registers. An edict ordered Hongzheng to collate them.

s0072.literal: At that time the court debated moving the capital; court gentlemen whose families were in Jingzhou all did not wish to move—only Hongzheng and the Minister of Works Wang Pou spoke to Emperor Yuan: "If gentry above the age of full study who slightly know past and present understand that where an emperor dwells has no fixed place, there is nothing to doubt.
s0072.idiomatic: At that time the court debated moving the capital. Court gentlemen whose families were in Jingzhou all wished to stay—only Hongzheng and Minister of Works Wang Pou said to Emperor Yuan, "Gentry of full learning who know past and present understand that an emperor's seat has no fixed place. There is nothing to doubt.

s0073.literal: As for the black-haired masses, if they have not seen the imperial carriage enter Jianye, they will think this a feudal prince among the states and not yet call you Son of Heaven.
s0073.idiomatic: As for the common people, if they have not seen the imperial carriage enter Jianye, they will think you a feudal prince among the states and not yet call you Son of Heaven.

s0074.literal: Now you should follow the people's hearts and accord with the hope of the four seas."
s0074.idiomatic: Now you should follow the people's hearts and accord with the hope of the four seas."

s0075.literal: At that time men of Jing and Shanxi all said Wang and Zhou were both easterners wishing to go east and feared it was not a good plan.
s0075.idiomatic: At that time men of Jing and Shanxi all said Wang and Zhou were easterners who wished to go east and feared it was not a good plan.

s0076.literal: Hongzheng confronted them face to face and said: "If easterners urge east and you call it a bad plan, you westerners wish west—how is that a good plan?"
s0076.idiomatic: Hongzheng confronted them and said, "If easterners urge east and you call it a bad plan, you westerners wish west—how is that a good plan?"

s0077.literal: Emperor Yuan then laughed greatly at this and in the end did not return the capital.
s0077.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan laughed greatly at this and in the end did not return the capital.

s0078.literal: When Jiangling fell, Hongzheng broke through the siege and came out, returning to the capital; Emperor Jing made him chief clerk to Grand Marshal Wang Sengbian, acting for Yang province affairs.
s0078.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, Hongzheng broke through the siege and returned to the capital. Emperor Jing made him chief clerk to Grand Marshal Wang Sengbian, acting for Yang province.

s0079.literal: In the first year of Taiping he was appointed Palace Attendant and concurrently National University Libationer, promoted to Minister of Ceremonies and Minister of Justice.
s0079.idiomatic: In Taiping year 1 (556) he was made palace attendant and concurrently national university libationer, then promoted to minister of ceremonies and minister of justice.

s0080.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, [Hongzheng] was appointed Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
s0080.idiomatic: When the Founder received the abdication, Hongzheng was made grand mentor to the heir apparent.

s0081.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng he was promoted to Palace Attendant and National University Libationer and went to Chang'an to welcome Emperor Xuan.
s0081.idiomatic: In Tiancheng year 1 (560) he was promoted to palace attendant and national university libationer and went to Chang'an to welcome Emperor Xuan.

s0082.literal: In the third year he returned from Zhou; an edict appointed him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon and made him concurrently Grand Steward of Cixun.
s0082.idiomatic: In year 3 he returned from Zhou. An edict made him grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon and concurrently grand steward of Cixun.

s0083.literal: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, [Hongzheng] concurrently held the post of Minister of Justice and oversaw the five rites.
s0083.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, he concurrently served as minister of justice and oversaw the five rites.

s0084.literal: He was then appointed Chief Clerk to the Grand Tutor and made Bright-Prestige General.
s0084.idiomatic: He was then made chief clerk to the grand tutor and bright-prestige general.

s0085.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he was promoted to Special Grand Master, again held the National University Libationership, and was Chief Rectifier for Yu province; he was given attendants.
s0085.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he was promoted to special grand master, again made national university libationer, and chief rectifier for Yu province; he was given attendants.

s0086.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; libationer and chief rectifier as before.
s0086.idiomatic: In Taijian year 5 (573) he was made right vice director of the secretariat, with libationer and chief rectifier unchanged.

s0087.literal: Soon an edict ordered him to attend the Eastern Palace to lecture on the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety.
s0087.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered him to attend the Eastern Palace to lecture on the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety.

s0088.literal: The Heir Apparent, because Hongzheng was an old minister of the court whose virtue and standing had long been weighty, therefore lowered his manner and bent ritual, spread the classics and asked for benefit—there was the respect due a teacher.
s0088.idiomatic: The heir apparent, because Hongzheng was an old minister whose virtue and standing were weighty, lowered his manner and bent ritual, spread the classics and asked for instruction—with the respect due a teacher.

s0089.literal: Hongzheng was especially skilled in dark discourse and also understood Buddhist scriptures; though great scholars and famous monks, none failed to ask him to resolve doubts.
s0089.idiomatic: Hongzheng was especially skilled in dark discourse and also understood Buddhist scriptures. Great scholars and famous monks all came to him to resolve doubts.

s0090.literal: In the sixth year he died in office, aged seventy-nine.
s0090.idiomatic: In year 6 he died in office, aged seventy-nine.

s0091.literal: An edict said: "To pursue the distant and praise virtue—indeed there is a constant rule.
s0091.idiomatic: An edict said, "To pursue the distant and praise virtue—indeed there is a constant rule.

s0092.literal: The late Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent National University Libationer and Chief Rectifier for Yu province, Hongzheng—his knowledge and breadth were deep and settled, his arts and calling complete; forest of letters and storehouse of righteousness, elder of the state and teacher of the people; the Way shone at the school gate, his repute high in the ritual hall; suddenly he has fallen—We are deeply moved.
s0092.idiomatic: The late right vice director of the secretariat, concurrent national university libationer and chief rectifier for Yu province, Hongzheng—his knowledge was deep and settled, his arts complete; a forest of letters and storehouse of righteousness, elder of the state and teacher of the people; the Way shone at the school gate, his repute high in the ritual hall. Suddenly he has fallen—we are deeply moved.

s0093.literal: He may be posthumously made Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat; what the funeral requires shall be supplied in measured addition."
s0093.idiomatic: He may be posthumously made palace attendant and director of the secretariat. What the funeral requires shall be supplied in full measure."

s0094.literal: He then went out to attend the mourning in person.
s0094.idiomatic: The Emperor then went out to mourn him in person.

s0096.literal: His writings include sixteen scrolls of Exegesis and Commentary on the Book of Changes, eleven scrolls of Commentary on the Analects, eight scrolls of Commentary on Zhuangzi, five scrolls of Commentary on the Laozi, two scrolls of Commentary on the Classic of Filial Piety, and twenty scrolls of collected works—in circulation in the world.
s0096.idiomatic: His writings include sixteen scrolls of commentary on the Book of Changes, eleven on the Analects, eight on Zhuangzi, five on the Laozi, two on the Classic of Filial Piety, and twenty scrolls of collected works—in circulation in the world.

s0097.literal: His son Fen rose to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
s0097.idiomatic: His son Fen rose to gentleman of the ministry of personnel.

s0098.literal: Hongzheng had two younger brothers: Hongrang and Hongzhi.
s0098.idiomatic: Hongzheng had two younger brothers: Hongrang and Hongzhi.

s0099.literal: Hongrang was plain and simple by nature, broadly learned and master of many subjects; in the first year of Tiancheng, as a commoner he held the post of Minister of Ceremonies and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with golden seal and purple ribbon.
s0099.idiomatic: Hongrang was plain and simple by nature, broadly learned and master of many subjects. In Tiancheng year 1 (560), though a commoner, he held the posts of minister of ceremonies and grand master of splendid happiness, with golden seal and purple ribbon.

s0100.literal: Hongzhi, styled Sifang, was clever and keen from childhood.
s0100.idiomatic: Hongzhi, styled Sifang, was clever and keen from childhood.
